descriptionChirho: Additive particle indicating inclusion of an additional item or person, equivalent to English 'also, too'; frequently paired with waw-conjunctive as וְאַף 'and also'.
Emphatic affirmative particle reinforcing a statement, equivalent to English 'indeed, surely, yea, certainly'; often at the head of a clause for rhetorical emphasis.

Rhetorical particle introducing an a fortiori argument ('how much more' or 'how much less'), often in the pattern אַף כִּי; conveys that if something is true in a lesser case, it is certainly true in a greater case, or vice versa.
Scalar particle highlighting an extreme or unexpected case, equivalent to English 'even'; emphasizes that the item mentioned goes beyond what is expected.
Discourse-connective particle adding a further point that strengthens or supplements the preceding statement, equivalent to English 'moreover, furthermore, what is more'.
Emphatic particle used in rhetorical or genuine questions, often with interrogative הֲ, expressing surprise or challenging a claim: 'is it indeed so?', 'will you really?'.
Rare adversative or contrastive use of the particle, equivalent to English 'yet, but, however', marking a contrast with the preceding statement.
